improvements.title: Pin the FULL option-byte profile (WRP both banks, OEM1/OEM2 lock, BOOT_LOCK, BOR_LEV, nBOOT0/nSWBOOT0, HDP) and escalate a persistent post-lock mismatch from halt to wipe
improvements.threat: Option-byte tamper / RDP regression in the RDP-0→RDP-2 transit window and after lock: a unit whose WRP was cleared before the RDP-2 burn, an OEM1/OEM2 RDP-regression password planted at the factory or in transit, a SWAP_BANK flip (NS-programmable without BOOT_LOCK), or a lowered BOR level (the μ-Glitch L5 attack needed to defeat BoD) — none of which today's tz-1 tripwire or Phase A can see; and a halted (not wiped) device leaves secrets in place for a second physical attempt.
improvements.proposal: (1) Run the deferred silicon pin on sacrificial U585 dies for WRP1AR/WRP2AR, NSSR.OEM1LOCK/OEM2LOCK, SECBOOTADD0R.BOOT_LOCK, OPTR.BOR_LEV/nBOOT0/nSWBOOT0/SWAP_BANK and SECWM1R2.HDP1 polarity, then flip `WRP1A_MASK_PINNED`, `OEM_LOCK_MASK_PINNED` and `require_boot_lock` to true in BOTH `SHIP_PROFILE_U585`/`LOCKED_PROFILE_U585` and widen `optr_matches_ship` to an exact OPTR mask (Trezor compares the whole OPTR constant). (2) FSBL tz-1 compares the full set every boot (≈ +100 B). (3) First-boot Phase A asserts OEMxLOCK clear and BOOT_LOCK set BEFORE the RDP=0xCC burn (OEM keys cannot be cleared after RDP-2) and the factory ship profile JSON lists OEM1KEYR/OEM2KEYR=0xFFFFFFFF + lock bits for the SWD verifier. (4) Secure world: once journal ALL_DONE, a 2-pass persistent mismatch on ANY pinned field drives `tzic::trigger_intrusion_wipe` (admin-wipe both SEs + page 126 erase) instead of `secure_log!`; FSBL keeps halt (no SE driver there).
improvements.rationale: Invariant #10 rests on 'WRP set before RDP-2'; today no software can tell a unit where that ordering was violated from a good one, and OEM keys are the documented U5 path to make RDP-2 reversible. Trezor's shipped boardloader treats any divergence from the pinned profile as 'first boot OR hardware fault OR exploit attempt' and destroys the BHK; pq1's halt is strictly weaker for a stolen device. Pinning the layout is a one-time silicon receipt; the comparator code already exists host-tested in shared::lockdown.

improvements.title: FSBL fault-injection delta before the WRP freeze: TRNG online, random pre-gate delays, default-poisoned branch target, duplicated verdicts, MSPLIM, WOTS-checksum redundancy, and a release-ELF survival gate
improvements.threat: Voltage/EM glitch on the FSBL's deterministic-timing verify chain (HSI16, fixed `wait_random` length) to boot an unsigned slot or skip tz-1; WOTS checksum fault on the on-device C10 VERIFIER (Wagner et al. 2023/2025: affects verification, not just signing) to accept a forged firmware signature; LTO/opt-level-s folding the redundant compares away so the sentinel discipline exists only in source.
improvements.proposal: (a) Bring the RNG peripheral up in the FSBL (RCC AHB2 clock + CONDRST sequence already written in secure/src/hw/rng.rs) so `fi::rng_byte` returns TRNG bytes instead of 0x42; fall back to halt, not to a constant. (b) Insert `wait_random()` immediately before each `check_true_into_sentinel` call in `filter_valid`/`verify_images`/tz-1 and before the branch. (c) Replace the `Option`/let-else slot selection with a volatile branch target initialised to a poison address (e.g. 0xFFFF_FFFE → HardFault) and assigned only after the last gate, plus a duplicated slot/verdict pair compared under `black_box` right before `branch::into_slot`. (d) Set MSPLIM in the FSBL reset path (currently 'no MSPLIM'). (e) In the FSBL's C10 verify (and the signer), recompute the WOTS checksum/target-sum from the message digest a second time via an independent code path and compare before the hypertree walk (the 2023/1572 countermeasure class). (f) Add a CI gate that disassembles the release FSBL/secure ELFs and asserts the double-evaluate + compare sequences survived (TF-M's explicit warning), using the existing `rainbow` instruction-skip sweep on `fsbl::verify_images`/`filter_valid` (#591).
improvements.rationale: Every byte of the FSBL becomes physically permanent at RDP-2; this is the last window to add FI hardening to the only code the user ever trusts. The gate currently needs ~2 coordinated faults but with fixed timing an attacker can characterise both offsets offline; Trezor's boardloader adds `fih_delay()` before every ensure and sets `next_stage_addr` last for exactly this reason.

improvements.title: Measurement-bound secret release (DICE-style): seal the SE050 BHK wrap / an extra entropy share to H(DHUK, FSBL-measured secure-image digest) so a modified secure image cannot reconstruct the seed even with full MCU code execution
improvements.threat: Malicious or implanted firmware on the MCU after sale (RDP downgrade by glitch, or a pre-sale reflash the user did not SWD-verify) that passes or skips the FSBL fingerprint check: today any code on the die can recompute the DHUK-derived PBS/BHK material and unlock both SEs — the fingerprint is a human-checked indicator, not a cryptographic gate (the Donjon Safe 3 lesson: pairing-secret possession proves access to a secret, not the software running).
improvements.proposal: The FSBL (which already holds the verified secure digest `secure_digest` at the branch) hands that digest forward in a typed SRAM handoff block; early secure-world boot derives `seal_key = SAES-CMAC(DHUK, 'pq1-seal-v1' || secure_digest)` and uses it (not plain DHUK) as the wrap key for page 126 (SE050 BHK) and as a third XOR share of the entropy reconstruction (`entropy = half_O ⊕ half_E ⊕ KDF(seal_key)`), or at minimum as the OPTIGA PBS salt derivation input. A legitimate firmware update becomes a journaled re-seal: the OLD image (still running, PIN-unlocked, after CMD_FW_COMMIT verified the new manifest) re-wraps page 126 under the NEW image's signed `secure_hash` from the manifest, exactly like the Phase-B transport→final rotation journal on page 127. The FSBL additionally zeroes the handoff block's SRAM alias before any NS code runs.
improvements.rationale: This is the strongest shipped primitive against malicious firmware (Tillitis TKey CDI, DICE/Caliptra): it converts the 8-word fingerprint from 'the user must notice' into 'wrong code cannot unwrap'. It needs no new SE primitive, no classical signer, no new per-signature state, and reuses the existing journal machinery. Because it consumes FSBL bytes (handoff block) and the FSBL freezes at RDP-2, the DECISION must be taken before the #540 cutover even if implementation lands later.

improvements.proposal: (1) Turn docs/security/user-device-verification.md into code: `pq1-verify` (host, probe-rs/STM32_Programmer_CLI connect-under-reset, no VBAT) dumps both banks + OTP + every option-byte register (incl. improvements.title: Boot-time dual-SE attestation with factory-pinned UIDs plus a C10 MCU attestation command (AuthenticateDevice analogue), bound to the FSBL measurement
improvements.threat: Chip swap (OPTIGA or SE050) in transit or after sale; a cloned board with genuine-looking firmware; a stolen device re-shelled around a fresh MCU — none detected today because no code reads an SE attestation object, pins SE UIDs, or lets the companion challenge the unit remotely.
improvements.proposal: (1) At boot, after SCP03/Shielded sessions are up: read OPTIGA UID (0xE0C2) and the SE050 chipId, compare against the per-device binding record (already specified 3× in threat-model §9.4 rows; store the SHA-256 anchor in the OTP birth record from BOOT-04); mismatch after first-boot ALL_DONE → admin-wipe path. Verify a fresh-nonce signature from each SE's factory cert (OPTIGA 0xE0E3 type-0x12 device cert already present; SE050 C-class 0xF0000013) against the Infineon/NXP roots pinned in the image — the SE is the signer, so invariant #5 (no classical signer in the WALLET) holds; document that these are vendor-mandated verifications like dbgen's EAS fence. (2) Add `CMD_ATTEST_DEVICE`: the secure world signs `'pq1-attest:' || compactsize(challenge) || challenge || secure_digest` with a SPHINCS+C10 key derived per use from SAES-CMAC(DHUK, 'attest') (never stored), whose public key the factory certifies into the per-unit record; companion verifies chain + both SE proofs; stream the 4008-B signature in APDU chunks. (3) Bind: the attestation message includes the FSBL-forwarded secure digest (BOOT-03 handoff), so the proof says 'this die, these SEs, this measured image'.
improvements.rationale: Trezor (ML-DSA-44 MCU cert + OPTIGA + TROPIC01), Ledger (SE genuine check) and BitBox (device attestation) all ship post-sale genuineness checks; pq1 has none, so a swapped SE or cloned unit is invisible once the SWD window has passed. Donjon showed attestation keyed from an MCU-held secret only proves possession — hence binding to the measurement and to DHUK (per-die, RDP-2-only final) rather than a flash secret.

improvements.title: Make the production-silent boot checks fatal (RDP<L2, SECBOOTADD0, die-id), gate the irreversible first-boot ceremony on reset cause, and declare RDP-1 a fatal wipe state
improvements.threat: A production image (no debug-log) in which an RDP regression before ALL_DONE, a redirected SECBOOTADD0, or a non-rev-U / counterfeit die produces NO observable effect because the checks compile to nothing; a glitch- or watchdog-induced reset mid-Phase-A that lets the RDP=0xCC burn run from a corrupted state; and a unit stranded at RDP-1 (RDP Freeze: cycle-accurate RAM/register capture of seed material in S-SRAM).
improvements.proposal: (1) Replace `secure_log!`-only outcomes in main.rs:1240-1290 and die_id with a `FihBool` verdict that halts (pre-ALL_DONE) or escalates to the intrusion-wipe path (post-ALL_DONE) in `mode-production`; resolve #192 by making `rdp-enforce-halt` the production default with the self-lock exemption expressed as 'RDP-0 is allowed ONLY while the page-127 journal is blank'. (2) Read RCC_CSR reset flags at Phase A entry: allow the RDP burn only after a POR/BOR/pin reset (`PINRSTF|BORRSTF` exactly, Trezor's rule), refuse and re-prompt after SFTRST/IWDG/WWDG/OBL/LPWR resets; clear flags via RMVF. (3) Treat an observed RDP level 1 (0xDC/0.5 or any non-0xAA/0xCC) as fatal: pre-ALL_DONE → halt with an E08xx code and refuse the burn; post-ALL_DONE → wipe. (4) Add a host test that greps the production cfg for any `secure_log!`-only security verdict (the pattern that produced this gap).

improvements.title: Sign and measure the FULL slot capacity (padding included) and pin the state of every page outside the measured images (erased-check or first-boot random fill), so no unmeasured flash can host an implant stage or stale code
improvements.threat: A second-stage payload, a stale previous image, or planted data parked in the tail of a slot, in a free bank-2 page, or in the unused manifest-B/boot-state pages: the FSBL hashes only `secure_len`/`ns_len` bytes, so the 8-word fingerprint and the SWD diff both stay identical while the device carries attacker bytes that a glitched or trampolined boot can reach.
improvements.proposal: (1) Manifest v6 (when adopted) signs hashes over the full `SLOT_SECURE_CAPACITY`/`SLOT_NS_CAPACITY` (image + deterministic 0xFF padding), and `verify_images` hashes the full capacity — Trezor's `check_image_contents` rule — or, cheaper for the FSBL budget, after hashing the image the FSBL erase-checks (reads == 0xFFFFFFFF) every remaining word of both slots and halts otherwise. (2) Every page not owned by the geometry registry (free pages, inactive manifest, retired boot-state page) must read erased at boot; the registry crate gains an `expect_erased` set checked by the FSBL and by `pq1-verify` (BOOT-04). (3) Optional Krux variant: first boot fills free pages with TRNG data and pins their SHA-256 in page 127 so a later change flips the fingerprint; prefer the erased-check because it needs no per-unit state.
improvements.rationale: Measured boot that leaves unmeasured flash is a known hole (Ledger LSB-002's code-cave lived in unused/duplicated bytes; Krux fills free blocks for this reason). The HASH peripheral makes reading 2 MB cheap relative to the 2.9 s C10 verify, and the check is pure reads inside the immutable range.

improvements.title: HDP hide-protection over the per-device secret pages after the BHK/salt are latched, with the FSBL/first-boot stage as the only reader
improvements.threat: A runtime secure-world bug (NSC parser, SE driver, ERC-7730 renderer) or a mid-session glitch reading page 126 (DHUK-wrapped SE050 BHK) / page 127 (journal + OPTIGA PBS salt) and leaking or replaying them; today those pages stay readable by the entire secure runtime for the whole power cycle.
improvements.proposal: Relocate the read-once-per-boot pages (126 BHK wrap, 127 journal/salt; NOT 123/124 which are written at runtime) into an HDP-capable region — HDP1 covers a contiguous range from the SECWM1 start, so either pages immediately after the FSBL (pages 5..6 of bank 1, inside the frozen registry's spare) or HDP2 over the low pages of bank 2 — and set `SECHDPCR.HDP1_ACCDIS`/`HDP2_ACCDIS` in early secure boot right after the BHK is loaded into TAMP BKP0R-7R + BHKLOCK and the PBS salt is consumed, making them invisible to all code (even secure) until the next reset. First-boot Phase B writes the journal BEFORE disabling access; the secure-world RDP/SECBOOTADD0 checks (BOOT-06) also confirm HDP is set. Pin the HDP1 polarity (flash.rs:79) in the BOOT-01 silicon ceremony.
improvements.rationale: Trezor's secret sector (BHK, master-key slots, counters, device cert) is exactly this shape and is HDP-hidden before every stage hand-off; pq1 has zero HDP/SECHDPCR usage. pq1 already does the hard half (BHK into TAMP registers + BHKLOCK), so hiding the source pages is the natural completion and removes page 126/127 from the reach of every later secure-world bug.

HDP covers reads for the rest of the boot only (resets re-expose), so it complements, not replaces, the wrap. The first-boot RDP burn itself is unaffected (OPTR is not in flash pages). If HDP1 start is forced to the SECWM start (page 0), the FSBL range would also become hidden after the FSBL stage — acceptable (it is already executed) but the secure-world advisory measured_boot re-hash of the FSBL range would stop working; it is compiled out of production anyway.

improvements.title: 2-of-3 SPHINCS+C10 vendor-key quorum in the FSBL, OTP hash-lock of the vendor key set, and an FSBL measurement field in every release receipt
improvements.threat: Single vendor-key compromise (one HSM, one insider) signs a malicious firmware that every FSBL accepts forever; a re-flashed FSBL at RDP-0 carrying a different vendor key is accepted by the signing tool's fingerprint check as long as the bundle matches; a release receipt that says 'bundle verified' proves nothing about which FSBL is on the part (demonstrated 2026-09-28, #742).
improvements.proposal: (1) Embed three C10 vendor public keys in the FSBL's named section and require any 2 distinct signatures (sigmask with exact-consumption + complement discipline, Trezor boot_header.c) over the manifest digest; `fwsign sign` becomes a two-ceremony flow with separately held seeds (threshold is at the key-set level, no classical CoSi). (2) Burn SHA-256 of the three-key set into an OTP word at factory and have both the FSBL (read-only, pre-branch) and `pq1-verify` (BOOT-04) compare it (#220). (3) Every release receipt and the signed release descriptor carry the FSBL ELF/flash digest the bundle was verified against, so the 'bundle under a different FSBL' case is a receipt mismatch (#742). Keep one verifier algorithm (invariant #5); measured cost is 0.375 s per verify chain on pq1 at HSI16, so 2 signatures ≈ +0.4 s boot.
improvements.rationale: Every surveyed vendor with a reflashable second stage uses an m-of-n quorum (Trezor 2-of-3, Foundation 2-of-4); pq1's FSBL is the one component that can never be patched, so the key-management failure mode it accepts must be the smallest. OTP-locking the key set is the only way to make the verify-before-first-power diff detect a swapped-vendor FSBL without comparing the whole FSBL image.

Threshold does not help if both signing seeds are derived from one root — the process must enforce independent generation.

improvements.title: Feasibility study: in-field electrical self-fingerprint of the board (TSC capacitance of display/SE nets, PDN response via ADC+TIM stimulus, panel-rail current) enrolled at the RDP-0 verification and re-checked before unlock
improvements.threat: Hardware implants and probes the firmware cannot see: a passive tap on the LCD SPI (the Grand/Nano X implant class — the display is a plaintext sink even though the device is otherwise all-internal-flash), an EM/laser FI probe parked over the package, a swapped PCB or added IC — all invisible to measured boot, option-byte checks and SE attestation.
improvements.proposal: Run a bench study on pq1 silicon (not an EVT change first): (1) STM32U585 TSC charge-transfer counts on candidate nets that can be sampled without a dedicated electrode (LCD SCK/MOSI/CS PA5/PA7/PA4 between frames, SE I2C lines during bus idle, the NC pins PA6/PC13), temperature-compensated with the internal temp sensor; (2) ADC1/ADC4 sampling of VDD/VDDA ripple while the consumption-mask TIM drives a known stimulus — a cheap on-chip proxy for ImpedanceVerif's PDN response; (3) if the EVT allows, a sense resistor on the LCM_EN/backlight rail read by ADC (panel-rail current signature vs. an added load). Enrol the baseline during the first-boot ceremony (after the user's SWD verification and before RDP-2), seal it in page 127/SE, and compare at boot and before each sign with a Wasserstein/Fréchet distance; a large distance refuses to unlock (never wipes — FPR is unknown). Deliverable is a go/no-go with measured intra-unit drift vs. probe-clip/implant deltas.
improvements.rationale: This is the only mechanism in the literature by which a device can notice an implant or a probe from the inside, and no vendor ships it; the user explicitly asked for it. The U585 already has the peripherals (TSC, ADC, COMP, OPAMP, TIM) and pq1 already owns a secure TIM stimulus source (consumption mask). Honest limit stated up front: a self-enrolled baseline cannot catch an implant inserted BEFORE enrolment — which is exactly why enrolment must sit after the RDP-0 verify-before-first-power step and why BOOT-04 (per-unit factory PDN/Z-profile with a VNA, offline) is the complementary supply-chain half.
